stop_condition: Each of the nine r2 findings is ruled on against the shipped artifact by the mechanism its resolution record claims, with an executed negative control wherever the claim is behavioural; the stale-absolute class is swept over every assertion the fix round added; and no critical or high finding remains in green_check_run, the green-check envelope, or the L1 tier.

findings.evidence: Demonstrated with a negative control, against the verbatim-extracted shipped green_check_run (awk 'NR>=13200 && NR<=13321'), driven in memory under set -e on this host (timeout ABSENT, gtimeout ABSENT, bash 3.2.57). CAP FIRED: cap=2 over `sleep 10` returned "124 watchdog" at elapsed=4s. CAP DID NOT FIRE: cap=20 over `exit 124` returned "124 watchdog" at elapsed=2s. Byte-identical returns. The logs are identical in shape too: both end with the same [green_check_run] NOTE, which is appended on EVERY watchdog run whether or not the cap fired, the only difference being the configured cap value substituted into the boilerplate (2s vs 20s) -- which reports configuration, not firing. Controls that anchor the probe: cap=20 over `sleep 1; exit 0` -> "0 watchdog" at 1s (no false cap, no idle-out); cap=20 over `sleep 1; exit 3` -> "3 watchdog" (real rc preserved); cap=2 over a grandchild-spawning tree -> "124 watchdog" at 4s with zero leaked processes. Reachability of the false claim confirmed: usage() spans 3032-3690 and the text renders at line 617 of `bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh --help`.
findings.description: THE SHIPPED --help CONTRACT STATES A PROPERTY THE CODE DOES NOT HAVE: 'The envelope's `dispatch` field names which mechanism bounded THIS run ... so a 124 this cap produced is never confused with one the test runner produced on its own.' The same claim is repeated in two code comments. `dispatch` reports which mechanism WRAPPED the run, never which one FIRED; on the timeout/gtimeout branches it is structurally incapable of the distinction. THIS IS A RECORDED LESSON THE FIX ROUND WAS TWO GREPS FROM. LESSONS.md:282 (recorded 2026-09-13, one day before this work): 'the loop must carry TWO escapes of its own -- a wall-clock deadline, and a liveness check on the producer -- and must print WHICH escape fired, so "the run finished" stays distinguishable from "the run died". A waiter that cannot say why it stopped is the same defect family as a measurement that did not happen looking identical to one that passed.' The fix implements escapes 1 and 2 and omits requirement 3. FOR THE RECORD, BOTH CITATION ERRORS: the coordinator's fix brief named this 'the UNBOUNDED-WAITER family in LESSONS.md' and that phrase appears nowhere (`grep -i unbounded LESSONS.md` returns zero hits at this tree); the implementer grepped for that invented label, got zero, and concluded 'there is no such entry' -- a keyword-absence read as a concept-absence. The lesson exists at :282 and is directly on point. The fix correctly rests on the demonstrated defect and on run_with_timeout (03tf) as a real reference, not on the bad citation, but the third requirement was lost with it. WHY IT MATTERS: rc=124 -> result="red", and on a unit-bound task at --phase before that is cannot_start_from_green exit 2 instructing the agent 'Do NOT implement. Open the red baseline as its own task (typed bug).' An agent that reads the --help contract, sees exit_code=124 and dispatch=watchdog, and believes the documented disambiguation files a bug for a red baseline that does not exist -- exactly the outcome R2-F2(2) was raised to prevent. R2-F6's new 50-line log tail, the one place a reader would look, is silent on the single fact that matters. REPAIR IS ONE OF EXACTLY TWO OPTIONS, NOT A THIRD: (1) surface the ground truth green_check_run already computes -- the $wd_marker presence on the watchdog branch, and rc==124 AND elapsed>=cap on the timeout/gtimeout branches -- as a `timed_out` boolean in the envelope; or (2) delete the claim from all three surfaces. Narrowing or softening the wording while leaving it standing is not option three.

findings.evidence: The header justifies 4500 with: 'it stays under the STOP HOOK's EXTERNAL 1320s wall-clock kill, a constraint this command has no analogue of (green-check is not invoked by any hook with its own external kill).' The hook clause is true and the conclusion does not follow. Grepped every green-check invocation in the repo: the ONLY callers anywhere are the three implementer prompts added in this same change set -- backend.md:152, frontend.md:83, devops.md:82 -- each a plain foreground agent Bash call ('bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh green-check $TASK_ID --phase before'). No hook invokes it; that is precisely why the hook-scoped analysis misses the binding constraint. The Bash tool in this harness carries a hard external ceiling of 600000ms maximum, 120000ms default. Independently corroborated by the coordinator this session: a full L1 tier run inside a subagent is killed by the harness at approximately 14 of 63 specs.
findings.description: THE INTERNAL CAP SHIPS AT 7.5x THE MAXIMUM EXTERNAL CEILING OF ITS ONLY DOCUMENTED CALLER (37.5x the default), so the watchdog that is the centerpiece of the R2-F2 fix is UNREACHABLE in the documented invocation path: the harness kill always wins first, with teardown semantics nobody here has characterised -- a PID-only kill would orphan the `bash -c "$cmd"` tree, the worse failure mode the watchdog exists to prevent. THIS REPO ALREADY MADE AND RECORDED THIS EXACT MISTAKE, in the paragraph IMMEDIATELY BELOW the measured figures the green-check header cites. verify-before-stop.sh:136-147: 'this value was briefly raised to 6000 (reasoning: size the internal cap to cover the suite, with headroom over contention) -- a real, well-measured fix to the WRONG layer. At any internal value above ~1300s the external kill always fires first regardless, so the internal watchdog above becomes unreachable code and the worse (possibly-orphaning) failure mode always wins instead of the clean one. Reverted same day.' The implementer read that comment for its numbers (1731/1777 uncontended, 3336-3913 contended) and not for its conclusion -- EBF-CORE's 'Read it COMPLETELY; skimming a reference is how you import its shape without its preconditions.' ON THE COORDINATOR'S QUESTION -- is 1.15x enough: that is the wrong question and that is the finding. 1.15x over 3913s would be defensible if 4500 were reachable; it is not. The sizing is also incoherent with its own justification: you cannot argue 'the caller is an unattended agent' to justify porting the watchdog and then argue 'there is no external kill' to justify 4500 -- those are claims about the same caller. THE FIGURE MUST BE SIZED AGAINST THE CALLER'S CEILING, NOT THE SUITE'S DURATION (the 03tf logic: stay below the external kill so the clean in-process teardown fires first -- e.g. ~540s with the three prompts instructing timeout: 600000 on the Bash call), AND THE HARNESS DEPENDENCY MUST BE STATED IN THE HEADER. The code currently names contention and project size as the variables and is silent on the one that actually binds. CORROBORATING, NOT PROVING: the implementer of this feature recorded green_before "none" / green_after "none" and did not run green-check on its own task; its stated reason (the task is unbound) is independently sufficient, so this is a straw in the wind, not evidence. SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: the watchdog IS reachable for an operator running green-check from a terminal; this finding is scoped to the documented agent caller. FALSIFIER: if implementer subagents can exceed 600s on a foreground Bash call in this harness, this collapses to a medium about the misleading sentence alone.

findings.evidence: usage() advertises 'override via the environment for a larger one'. Measured through the shipped ${VAR:-4500} guard (env set BEFORE the default line runs), against a genuinely GREEN 3-second suite, on the extracted shipped function: GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S='' -> "0 watchdog" GREEN (the :- default fires, 4500; correct); '30' -> "0 watchdog" GREEN (correct); '0' -> "124 watchdog" RED; 'abc' -> "124 watchdog" RED; '-5' -> "124 watchdog" RED; '4500s' -> "124 watchdog" RED. The last is the realistic typo: green_check_run itself writes "${GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S}s" two lines above, so the s-suffix is the form the code's own style invites. GNU coreutils documents 'A duration of 0 disables the associated timeout' (verified against the current GNU manual this session, not from memory), so GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S=0 runs UNBOUNDED on a host WITH timeout while killing immediately on a host without. CONTRAST, SAME REPO, SAME KIND OF KNOB, MEASURED: SPEC_TIMEOUT_S=0 -> run-tests.sh rc=2; SPEC_TIMEOUT_S=abc -> run-tests.sh rc=2.
findings.description: An advertised env override with no validation, whose malformed values silently convert a green suite into a red one -- and on a unit-bound task at --phase before, into cannot_start_from_green and an instruction to file a bug for a baseline that is not red. The 0 case is worse than red: it is host-dependent and one of its two arms REOPENS R2-F2's original defect (unbounded on a timeout host), while the only signal distinguishing the arms is the `dispatch` field whose disambiguating power R3-F1 shows is overstated. A figure whose behaviour depends on the host must say so, and this one does not. THE REMEDY IS TO COPY run-tests.sh's EXISTING SPEC_TIMEOUT_S VALIDATION VERBATIM (the `case "$X" in ''|*[!0-9]*) ... ; 0) ... esac` block, with its two distinct messages), not to write a new checker: the project already has the vocabulary, the refusal exit code, and the 'an unbounded spec is the mwrb defect' reasoning for the 0 arm. CORRECTION AGAINST MYSELF, RECORDED: my first probe reported the empty-string case as broken too. That was an artifact of setting the variable AFTER the ${VAR:-4500} line had already executed in the extracted copy. Re-probed faithfully with env set before the guard -- empty is FINE. Retracted.

findings.location: CONTRIBUTING.md, subsection 'Which EXISTING tests must I re-run before calling a change verified?' (the R2-F4 remedy)
findings.evidence: Answering the coordinator's question plainly: PROSE ONLY. No hook, spec, gate condition or CI job reads this subsection; nothing catches a future violation. That is defensible in itself -- R2-F4 asked for a mechanical FORM, not an enforcer, and the surrounding prose states the correct rule ('the specs that cover what I touched'). The defect is the shell snippet shipped with it, which looks executable. Ran it verbatim against this repo: it works HERE (430 candidates, noisy but non-empty). Then measured the failure mode, three primitives in isolation: `printf '' | xargs grep ...` -> grep never runs, rc=0, empty output; `grep -v ""` -> filters EVERY line, rc=1; end-to-end with an empty file list -> NO OUTPUT AT ALL. `git diff --name-only` with no revision argument compares the working tree to the INDEX, so it is empty the moment a contributor runs `git add` or `git commit`.
findings.description: In the state a contributor is most likely to be in -- work staged or committed, now verifying it -- the published recipe emits nothing, and BOTH halves fail silently in the same direction: no candidates from the empty xargs, and `grep -v "$(git diff --name-only)"` degenerating to `grep -v ""` which discards everything. The contributor reads zero output as 'no existing spec covers what I touched', which is the exact conclusion R2-F4 exists to prevent, delivered by R2-F4's own remedy. It is also the well-formed-EMPTY-answer shape CLAUDE.md already calls out about .beads/issues.jsonl. Fix: `git diff --name-only HEAD` (or --cached) and an explicit guard on the empty case. Two smaller nits in the same snippet: the extraction regex matches definitions as well as calls, so 'functions your diff CALLS that it does not define' is not what it computes (over-inclusion, the safe direction, but the prose overstates it); and /tmp/called.txt is a hardcoded shared path.

findings.evidence: The comment block added by this change set describes 'green-check.test.sh (57 assertions)'. The RESOLVED R2-F2 record posted on this same task for this same change set states '67/67 assertions exit 0' for that same file; Section 10 added the difference. Two numbers about one file, inside one change set, that disagree. The sibling figure IS accurate and was confirmed independently: validate-completion-green-fields.test.sh '(43 assertions)' -- I ran it standalone at this tree, 43/43 Passed, exit 0, 1.73s real (/usr/bin/time -p bash .claude/scripts/tests/validate-completion-green-fields.test.sh).
findings.description: Documentation staleness inside the delivered change set, against the project's standing rule that every number carries the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at. Nothing goes red -- EXPECTED_SPECS itself is 63 and correct, and the assertion count in the prose is not enforced -- but the comment's whole purpose is to record what each new spec is and how big it is, and this half of it describes a pre-Section-10 file. NOT A STALE-ABSOLUTE-CLASS DEFECT: EXPECTED_SPECS 61 -> 63 is a CORRECT hand-bump and I am correcting my own r2 phrasing, which lumped it with the R2-F1 class too loosely. The discriminator is not 'is it an absolute that needs bumping' but 'does the absolute stand in for a property that has a count-independent expression'. R2-F1's did; EXPECTED_SPECS's does not -- a count-independent version ('at least one spec') deletes the check, whose entire job is to notice a spec silently dropping out of discovery. It is an acknowledgement tripwire, and this bump carries 25 lines naming both new specs and why each exists, which is the conscious acknowledgement the tripwire is for.
